Severity ladder: what happens if outed? Border humiliation (severity 2), no imprisonment documented, no execution. Censorship/self-expression constraints — display of rainbow items not permitted; a visibly trans visitor risks scrutiny. But no criminal statute against trans presence.

Key: is there a universal-exposure measure? Border handling mocking — documented single incident. Censorship regime restricting expression of LGBT identity — this is arguably traveler-facing: displaying rainbow flags prohibited, drag performers cancelled, LGBT social media scrubbed. That's a real constraint on a trans visitor's public expression — but is it enforced against visitors? The foreign drag artist on tour in Aug 2026 found space shrinking — that's a visitor-facing data point.

No criminalization, no documented state violence, functioning-ish courts (one successful conversion-therapy payout — courts worked once). Social attitudes: 52% support same-sex marriage — moderate acceptance, generational split. No documented hostility toward trans visitors beyond border mocking.

Precedence ladder: worst documented feature = tier 3-ish? Censorship/hostile institutional environment, thin recourse (no anti-discrimination law, no hate crime, orgs can't register). Actually the institutional discrimination tied to legal gender marker is resident-facing. Border mockery = tier 2/3 (state officials derisive treatment but no detention).

Compared to anchors: 0.55-B is extended secondary screening, humiliation, refused admission possible, administrative penalties. Here we have border mockery and questioning — similar-ish but no refusal documented. 0.45 anchors involve universal exposure (registration, database flags) — here no such documented regime for visitors. 0.65 anchors have protections working partially — here courts gave one payout for conversion therapy (resident case), narrow remedy exists.

No criminalization + no documented trans violence + functioning-ish courts but no protections, hostile censorship climate, institutional discrimination, border derision. Rubric rule 21 band implication: "no criminalisation plus functioning institutions does not anchor at Reduced Risk; documented exposures subtract through band." Documented exposures here: border mistreatment (single incident), censorship of expression (national, active, 2024-2026), no recourse machinery.

But how much does censorship reach a trans visitor? A visibly trans tourist isn't displaying rainbow flags necessarily; but trans expression itself falls under "abnormal sexual behaviour" depiction bans and the shrinking space — foreign drag artist's shows affected. The climate suggests a visibly gender-nonconforming foreigner could face official friction. That's more social/institutional hostility than tier-1 state exposure.

Also no criminalization of same-sex conduct documented — actually "same-sex conduct has no legal protection" — meaning no protection, not criminalization. Dossier doesn't say same-sex conduct is criminal. So no sodomy statute.

Violence: single 2018 incident with guards fired — positive response. So street violence low/undocumented; note absence of evidence — but well-documented dossier overall (lots of detail) so silence on trans killings is moderately positive? The dossier explicitly says no trans killing figures carried — treat as undocumented per rule 16.

Care: gender-affirming care gated with parental consent — resident-facing; but for a visitor, emergency care? Not documented. HRT in-person purchase only (Dec 2022 online ban) — applies to anyone buying in country; a visitor needing estradiol must buy in person — mild exposure. Denial of care not documented for visitors.

Minors: travelling with a minor — a trans parent with a minor? Or trans minor? Gender-marker change for minors one province. Family-consent regime pushes disputes inside families — could matter for a trans teen with accepting parent? Actually parental consent requirement is for the trans person's own parents — an adult visitor whose parents are unsupportive doesn't need surgery abroad. For a trans minor travelling: care access gated, minor can't consent to surgery; puberty blockers available at seven centers (residents). Not much traveler-facing.

Score estimate: no criminalization, no state violence, no imprisonment risk, courts occasionally work, majority-leaning acceptance in polls, but: active censorship of LGBT expression, hostile institutions, no protections, border derision documented, no recourse for border mistreatment.

That sits around 0.55-0.62. Exposures: border humiliation (documented, single incident but state actors), national expression ban affecting visibly trans visitors (universal-ish exposure for visibly trans — the censored environment), no legal protections, thin recourse. Mitigations: no criminalization, no documented violence/state targeting, courts gave a record payout, guards fired for attack, polls supportive.

I'd say ~0.57. Consider anchor 0.55-B: extended secondary screening, refused entry possible, administrative — humiliation and financial cost, appeals slow. Our case: border mockery/questioning documented, no refusal documented, plus nationwide censorship climate beyond the border. Slightly worse than 0.55-B? 0.55-A has checkpoints holding people for verification — ours has questioning but no detention documented.

Compare 0.65 anchors: brief hold, released, complaint yields apology+compensation. Ours: mockery at border with no recourse mechanism stated (no anti-discrimination, no hate crime). So below 0.65 tier.

I'll go 0.58. Or 0.56. Let's settle 0.57.
